full_text:
The Sixth Vizier related an entertaining tale of discernment:

'In Damascus lived an intelligent and wealthy maiden named Layla, who was courted by two prominent suitors: the first was an officer of the guard who boasted constantly of his martial valor and high ancestry; the second was a quiet, modest physician who spent his days tending the sick in the public hospital.

To test their character before choosing her husband, Layla devised a clever test. She sent identical messages to both suitors: "Meet me at midnight beside the ancient well outside the city walls; wear your ordinary garments and bring the single tool that best represents your life’s purpose."

At midnight, both suitors arrived at the well.

The officer arrived riding a fiery stallion, clad in glittering chainmail, wielding a drawn scimitar, boasting: "With this sword, O lady, I can conquer cities, slay your enemies, and fill your halls with captive treasures!"

The physician arrived on foot, wearing a simple linen robe, carrying a leather pouch of medicinal herbs and a horn lantern.

Layla asked the physician: "And what can you accomplish with those herbs?"

The physician replied with gentle modesty: "With these herbs, my lady, I cannot conquer cities, but I can cool a burning fever, relieve the pain of a child, and bring peace to a troubled home."

Layla turned to the officer and said: "He who builds his love on the sword will bring the violence of the battlefield into his home; but he who heals suffering will nurture a household in peace." She gave her hand to the modest physician, celebrating a union founded on service and wisdom.'
moral: Boastful promises are empty wind; true worth is proven by modest character and unselfish action. [MR]
